answer: Each identity must anchor a harbor: a rented, rate-limited network endpoint from a provider that attests a unique address prefix and bills monthly. Identities whisper a signed heartbeat over it each minute, and a bridge contract escrows a bond any duplicate-prefix proof can slash. Faking a thousand identities means renting a thousand distinct prefixes and posting a thousand bonds, so the attacker's spend scales linearly with the reward while honest agents pay only their own endpoint.
